html:
The Narungga, also spelt Narangga, are an Aboriginal Australian people whose country is Yorke Peninsula in South Australia. Their language belongs to the Yura group, shared with neighbours such as the Kaurna across Gulf St Vincent and the Nukunu to the north.

The peninsula gave fish, shellfish, kangaroo and emu, and the people moved with the seasons between the coast and the scrub.

After South Australia was founded in 1836, sheep runs took the peninsula. Copper found at Kadina and Moonta in the early 1860s drew thousands of Cornish miners. In 1868 the Point Pearce mission was set up on the west coast of the peninsula, and it became the main home of Narungga families. Across Spencer Gulf lived the Barngarla.
